newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bank lending rises in August - ABI.
newsitem.headline: Italian bank lending rises in August - ABI.

text.p: Loans by Italian banks holding short-term deposits, accounting for all high street banks, grew 3.39 percent year-on-year in August to 855.0 trillion lire against growth of 3.62 percent in July, the Italian Banking Association ABI said.
Lire loans increased 5.8 percent year-on-year to 776.5 trillion lire against a 6.36 percent rise in July, provisional ABI data showed.
Foreign currency loans, however, fell 15.64 percent to 78.5 trillion lire following a 17.11 percent decline in July.

Total loans in the Italian banking system in July, the latest month for which data was available, including loans from banks holding medium-to-long term deposits, totalled 1,080.0 trillion lire, a rise of 2.08 percent on July 1995.
In June total loans grew 1.43 percent.
Total deposits in the banking system in June, according to latest ABI data, grew 4.62 percent year-on-year to 1,296.1 trillion lire.
